experiment: Qwen3.5-4B GSM8K paired GRPO vs Dr.GRPO

model.revision_source: huggingface_hub download metadata of the local checkpoint; all 13 file metadata entries, including both safetensors shards, carry the same commit hash

conversion: read the (question, answer) columns of the pinned source parquet
label = the text after the '####' marker of the answer, with commas removed and whitespace stripped
prompt = single user turn: 'Solve the following math problem step by step. The last line of your response must be exactly Answer: \boxed{answer}.\n\n' + question
write one JSON object per line as {"prompt": [{"role": "user", "content": ...}], "label": ...}
dataset.verified: re-running this conversion against the pinned source parquet reproduces the byte-identical JSONL; sampled prompts from both runs' rollout results were matched against that file

table_semantics.note: how every number in the PR body's two tables is derived from training_metrics_long.csv, so the tables can be rebuilt without any additional script
table_semantics.window: mean = all 200 steps; last20 = the final 20 steps
table_semantics.reward: arithmetic mean of rollout/raw_reward over the window
table_semantics.accuracy: sum(rollout/response_counts/correct) / sum(correct + incorrect) over all 200 steps
table_semantics.length: pooled: sum(per-step mean length * per-step count) / sum(count), skipping steps whose count for that class is 0
table_semantics.kl_loss: train/kl_loss is each algorithm's own objective-normalized component and is NOT comparable across algorithms: Dr.GRPO's value is sum(KL) / (N * B) because the optimizer-window scale T / (N * B) is applied before the metric reduction divides by T, while GRPO's is sum(KL) / T
table_semantics.reference_kl: train/reference_kl restates both runs as sum(KL) / T. Dr.GRPO's logged value is multiplied back by N * B (16 * 4096) and divided by that step's train/response_tokens; GRPO's logged value is already sum(KL) / T and is carried through unchanged
table_semantics.response_tokens: train/response_tokens is the per-step sum of response_length over the 16 responses, used as a proxy for sum(loss_mask); this recipe is single-turn text-only with no tool masking, and the proxy can only over-estimate T, never under-estimate it
table_semantics.grad_norm: mean and max of train/grad_norm over all 200 steps; p95 is the linearly interpolated 95th percentile of the sorted values
table_semantics.train_rollout_prob_abs_diff: per-step train/inference engine mismatch, |train prob - rollout prob| over the same tokens. Carried in the CSV as a health check on the paired runs; not used by any PR body table

excluded_from_git.rollout_result JSONL: pinned by a rollup sha256 over the 200 files used, in evidence_index.csv
